claims.claim: The U.S. Renewable Fuel Standard was created under the Energy Policy Act of 2005 and expanded by the Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007.
claims.episode_span: The U.S. Renewable Fuel Standard required refiners to blend increasing shares of corn ethanol and advanced biofuels
claims.source_title: Overview of the Renewable Fuel Standard Program | US EPA
claims.supporting_quote: The Renewable Fuel Standard program under the Clean Air Act was created under the Energy Policy Act of 2005 and further expanded by the Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007.

claims.claim: The EU's 2009 Renewable Energy Directive mandated that 10 percent of energy used in transport come from renewable sources by 2020.
claims.episode_span: and 10 percent renewable energy in transport across the EU by 2020
claims.source_title: EU: Renewable Transportation Fuel Policies - DieselNet
claims.supporting_quote: The Renewable Energy Directive (RED) set an overall target for renewable energy consumption of 20% by 2020 as well as a sub-target mandating 10% of the energy used for transport to be produced with renewable sources

claims.claim: In 2015 the EU amended its biofuel rules to address indirect land-use change and capped food- and feed-based biofuels in transport at 7 percent.
claims.episode_span: By 2015 the EU had introduced an indirect-land-use-change factor into its accounting rules and capped the contribution of food-based biofuels at 7 percent of transport energy.
claims.source_title: EU: Renewable Transportation Fuel Policies - DieselNet
claims.supporting_quote: a 2015 amendment capped the contribution of food- and feed-based biofuels used in transport to a maximum share of 7%

claims.claim: A February 2008 Science (Sciencexpress) paper led by Searchinger concluded that indirect land-use-change effects offset the direct emissions benefits of corn and cellulosic ethanol.
claims.episode_span: beginning with Searchinger’s Science paper and followed by multiple EU-commissioned reviews, recalculated emissions once peat-soil drainage and forest clearing were included
claims.source_title: Indirect land use change impacts of biofuels - Wikipedia
claims.supporting_quote: A controversial paper published in February 2008 in Sciencexpress by a team led by Searchinger from Princeton University concluded that such effects offset the (positive) direct effects of both corn and cellulosic ethanol

claims.claim: The 2015 Indonesian fires generated around 600 million tonnes of greenhouse gases, roughly equivalent to Germany's entire annual output.
claims.episode_span: The resulting smoke from peat fires in 2015 alone produced more CO2 in a single season than Germany’s annual industrial emissions.
claims.supporting_quote: The Global Fire Emissions Database reported that the 2015 Indonesian fires had generated around 600 million tonnes of greenhouse gases, an amount described as 'roughly equivalent to Germany's entire annual output'.
